title: Is lethal injection humane?
summary: Josh and Chuck examine lethal injection as the most common US execution method, covering its history from the nineteenth-century proposals and the 1972 Furman and 1976 Gregg rulings, the three-drug cocktail and its replacement by single-drug protocols (pentobarbital, propofol shortage), and the procedures on death row and death watch. They discuss last meals, execution witnesses and the public-execution history, executioners and medical ethics, botched executions and vein-finding problems, alternatives like inert gas asphyxiation and firing squads, and racial disparities in capital cases. The episode opens with news of Missouri's execution of Joseph Paul Franklin and Larry Flynt's opposition, and closes with a listener mail segment from Whitney in Utah.
topics: Eighth Amendment cruel and unusual punishment
Stuff You Should Know listener mail

segments.title: Opening banter and Joseph Paul Franklin execution news
segments.summary: The hosts introduce the episode and discuss the recent Missouri execution of Joseph Paul Franklin, Larry Flynt's opposition to it, and the state's secrecy over its execution drug supplier.

segments.title: History of lethal injection and abolition movements
segments.summary: The hosts trace abolition movements, the 1972 Furman ruling, the 1976 Gregg reversal, and how lethal injection was proposed in the nineteenth century and adopted in the US, with other countries following.
topics: Eighth Amendment cruel and unusual punishment

segments.title: Death penalty statistics and death row
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the number of states with the death penalty, de facto abolition, global use of lethal injection, current death row population, and concentration of executions in a few counties.

segments.title: Death watch and last meals
segments.summary: The hosts describe death watch, the final days before execution, and the varying rules on last meals, including Arkansas inmate Verry Leaf Fairchild's comment and historic pre-execution drinking.

segments.title: Witnesses and public execution history
segments.summary: The hosts explain who attends executions, the history of public hangings, the 1936 Kentucky execution of Rainey Bethea, and the reputable citizens program.

segments.title: Execution chamber procedures and drug cocktail
segments.summary: The hosts walk through the final steps: IV lines, the anti-room, executioners who do not know which line is live, and the original three-drug cocktail of anesthetic, paralytic and toxic agent.

segments.title: Single-drug protocols and drug shortages
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the shift to single-drug executions using pentobarbital, the manufacturer's objections, propofol and the hospital shortage, compounding pharmacies, and midazolam.

segments.title: Pet euthanasia comparison
segments.summary: Chuck mentions that his family dog was recently put down and notes the similar drug sequence used, with a brief remark on the topic.

segments.title: Medical ethics, vein access, and alternative methods
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the timeline from order to death, difficulty finding veins, the role of medical personnel and the AMA's hippocratic oath concerns, inert gas asphyxiation, firing squads, the guillotine, and racial disparities in capital cases.

segments.title: Listener mail from Whitney
segments.summary: Whitney, a band teacher from Provo, Utah, writes about how the podcast helped her through a stressful year.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts invite listeners to get in touch through social media and email, and point to the website for more information.
